children: CEO Jensen Huang reiterated on Thursday that he is “confident” in growing revenue 70% next year, adding that cybersecurity is likely to be the next major growth area for artificial intelligence.

Appearing at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Huang said that AI compute demand is staying strong and likely to remain well above supply. Last month, Nvidia management, including Huang, stunned
Street when they said they were expecting revenue to grow 70% year-over-year in 2027 and forecast more than 100% if demand were not constrained.

Additionally, Huang noted that Nvidia is expecting to capture a larger share of data center spending as it moves from selling GPUs into a full-stack AI factory system. The upcoming Vera Rubin system is priced at roughly $40,000, while previous systems for Blackwell and Hopper were priced at roughly $25,000 and $18,000, respectively.
He also noted that Nvidia is gaining share at Anthropic
, with Nvidia having invested in the Claude maker in November 2025.
AI as an asset class, next growth legs
Huang, ever the proponent for AI, said that AI compute has increasingly become an asset-backed class. The company has made several announcements with financial firms to finance AI infrastructure.
Its executives, including Huang, have repeatedly said Nvidia's systems have long-lasting value, given how much and how long they are used for and the attractive economics associated with them.

Aside from chatbots, data centers, robots, and more, Huang also touched on the next area of growth for AI, with cybersecurity at the forefront. The company has announced many partnerships with companies such as CrowdStrike
Other areas of growth include physical AI, including robots and autonomous driving, with Huang stating he expects “significant progress” in the next two or three years in the space.

title: Nvidia's Huang 'confident' in 70% growth, sees cybersecurity as next leg for AI
